title: Drift-tolerant delivery semantics for partial-output metering
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:

We currently attribute token credits at the point of emission for streaming responses. In several customer-reported scenarios (intermittent client disconnects, proxy buffering, midstream model handoffs and speculative decoding fallbacks) this causes either overcharging (orphaned credits) or undercounting when outputs are re-emitted after reconnection. Existing fixes focus on idempotency keys and finalization heuristics but do not address the more general case of delayed/duplicated fragments crossing rate-limit windows and quota reconciliations.

Goals:
- Define a delivery semantic that tolerates transient drift (reordered/duplicated fragments, delayed TCP/WS frames) while keeping accounting accurate and auditable.
- Ensure per-session rate-limiter state aligns with final credited tokens after reconnection or retry without opening a denial-of-service avenue.
- Provide deterministic audit traces that map emitted tokens to final ledger entries for customer-facing receipts.

Proposed approach (summary):
1) Introduce "delivery anchors": lightweight monotonic markers attached to streaming fragments. Anchors are agreed checkpoints that mark stable prefixes for which credits can be irrevocably reserved.
2) Emit provisional credits when fragments arrive, but tag them as provisional in the ledger. Provisional credits expire into permanent credits only when an anchor advances past the fragment. Expiry is deterministic (anchor seen / checkpoint committed / or TTL).
3) Maintain a small tombstone log per session for provisional fragments that were revoked or reissued. Tombstones provide provenance for audit and enable idempotent replay without double-crediting.
4) When a session reconnects, perform a quick checkpoint reconciliation: client reports last-seen anchor, server computes anchor-based diff and either: a) replays missing fragments without charging (if tombstoned), b) credits newly confirmed ranges, or c) issues a provisional rollback if ambiguous and not resolvable within a safety window.
5) Integrate anchor advancement with the rate-limiter: do not permanently deduct quota until anchor confirmation, but account for provisional reservations against a small protective buffer to avoid unbounded speculative consumption.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add integration tests that simulate: reorder, duplication, client reconnect with missing frames, and midstream model switch. Final ledger must match ground-truth token counts for the session in all scenarios.
- No new DB schema that requires multi-document transactions across customer ledgers (design must use append-only tombstones and idempotent commits).
- Rate-limiter must be updated to expose provisional reservation APIs and a bounded protective buffer mechanism.
- Audit trail: for any session, a sequence of anchors and tombstone entries can be exported and reconstruct the final token attribution deterministically.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not redesign the tokenizer or underlying token counting algorithm. It focuses on delivery semantics and ledger integration.

Trade-offs considered:
- Option A: eagerly commit credits on first emit (current model) — simple but leads to orphaned charges on unreconciled disconnects.
- Option B: fully defer credits until session close — avoids orphaned charges but increases risk of quota exhaustion spikes and opens DOS vectors.
- Chosen hybrid (anchors + provisional reservations) balances correctness and operational safety.

Implementation notes:
- Anchors are 64-bit monotonic counters scoped per session. They should be lightweight and piggybacked on existing fragment headers.
- Tombstones are append-only records with schema: session_id, anchor, fragment_range, reason, timestamp. Store in the metering append-only log sharded by customer.
- Provisional reservations decrement a per-session in-memory protective buffer (small, e.g., 5–10% of committed quota or a fixed token ceiling) to prevent large speculative consumption. If the buffer is exhausted, subsequent fragments are admitted but marked as pending with exponential backoff to the client.
- Reconciliation runs at reconnect or on regular background reconciliation window (configurable).

Risks and mitigations:
- Increased complexity of ledger reconciliation: mitigate via comprehensive unit/e2e tests and clear operational tooling to inspect anchor/tombstone state.
- Potential for abusive clients to hold provisional reservations: cap protective buffer and add heuristics (rate of anchor advancement, challenge/response) to throttle bad actors.

Next steps:
- Spike: prototype anchor propagation and provisional reservations in the streaming runtime (2 days).
- Design doc: detailed API and ledger schema (Confluence) — link below.
- Implementation: runtime changes + metering pipeline integration + tests (estimate 8 points).

2026-03-04 | Aisha Patel: Reviewed POC. Concern: protective buffer interacts with Dedicated capacity quotas — need to ensure reserved buffer doesn't bypass customer capacity limits. Suggest per-customer buffer caps and an opt-out flag for high-security customers.

2026-03-07 | Priya Nambiar (SRE): Observability plan: add anchor/tombstone metrics (per-customer rate, tombstone count, reconciliation failures) and a dashboard for in-flight provisional reservations.

2026-03-10 | Ethan Moore: Implemented tombstone append records and reconciliation fn. Local e2e sim (disconnect/replay) shows correct final ledger mapping. Pushing PR for initial review: github.com/redwood-inference/pr/4821
2026-03-14 | Security (J. Alvarez): Reviewed approach. No secrets/keys exposed. Recommend adding a small audit-only HMAC over anchors to prevent forged anchor replays from malicious clients.
